note: Original Copeak story content. Level labels are approximate learning targets; no examination-body endorsement is implied.

stories.title: The Empty Chair
stories.subtitle: 空いていた席
stories.description: A simple invitation changes an ordinary afternoon.

scenes.text: Every Sunday, Hana and her family ate lunch in the garden. There was always one empty chair beside the table.
scenes.ja: 毎週日曜日、ハナと家族は庭で昼食を食べました。テーブルの横にはいつも空いている椅子が一脚ありました。
scenes.alt: A warm family garden lunch with one clearly empty chair.

grammar.focus: There was always one empty chair beside the table.
grammar.note: There is / There was は「～がある・いた」を表します。主語は後ろの one empty chair です。

scenes.text: One day, Hana saw Mr. Ito sitting alone outside his house. His wife had died last winter, and he looked sad.
scenes.ja: ある日、ハナは伊藤さんが家の外で一人座っているのを見ました。妻は去年の冬に亡くなり、伊藤さんは悲しそうでした。
scenes.alt: An older neighbor sits alone on a porch as Hana notices him.

grammar.focus: Hana saw Mr. Ito sitting alone outside his house.
grammar.note: see + 人 + ～ing は「人が～しているのを見る」という知覚動詞の形です。

scenes.text: Hana walked to him and said, “Would you like to have lunch with us?” Mr. Ito was surprised, but he smiled.
scenes.ja: ハナは伊藤さんのところへ歩いて行き、「一緒にお昼を食べませんか」と言いました。伊藤さんは驚きましたが、笑顔になりました。
scenes.alt: Hana invites the elderly neighbor, who looks surprised and hopeful.

grammar.focus: Would you like to have lunch with us?
grammar.note: Would you like to ...? は相手を丁寧に誘う表現です。

scenes.text: At lunch, Mr. Ito told them funny stories about his younger days. Everyone laughed, and the empty chair was no longer empty.
scenes.ja: 昼食の席で、伊藤さんは若い頃の面白い話をしてくれました。みんなが笑い、空いていた椅子はもう空いていませんでした。
scenes.alt: All family members laugh with Mr. Ito at the once-empty garden chair.

grammar.focus: Mr. Ito told them funny stories about his younger days.
grammar.note: tell + 人 + 物語は「人に物語を話す」という第4文型です。

scenes.text: Before he went home, Mr. Ito said, “Thank you for remembering me.” Hana held his hand and answered, “Please come again.”
scenes.ja: 帰る前に伊藤さんは「私のことを覚えていてくれてありがとう」と言いました。ハナは彼の手を握り、「また来てください」と答えました。
scenes.alt: Mr. Ito and Hana gently hold hands at the garden gate.

grammar.focus: Thank you for remembering me.
grammar.note: Thank you for + 動詞のing形は「～してくれてありがとう」という表現です。

scenes.text: The next Sunday, Hana put one more chair in the garden. She knew there might be another person who needed a friend.
scenes.ja: 次の日曜日、ハナは庭にもう一脚椅子を置きました。友達を必要としている別の人がいるかもしれないと分かっていたからです。
scenes.alt: Two welcoming empty chairs at the sunny garden table, full of hope.

grammar.focus: there might be another person who needed a friend.
grammar.note: might be は「～かもしれない」。who needed a friend は person を説明する関係代名詞節です。

vocab.ja: 空の、誰も座っていない
vocab.detail: 中身がない状態を表す。an empty chair（空席）。
lonely（寂しい）とは異なり、alone は一人という状態を表します。
invite A to B（AをBへ招く）。本文では Would you like to ...? と丁寧に誘っています。
be surprised at / by ... で「～に驚く」。
以前はそうだったが、今はそうではないことを表します。
vocab.example: The chair was no longer empty.

vocab.detail: remember doing（～したことを覚えている）にも注意。
may より控えめな可能性を表すことがあります。
vocab.example: Another person might need a friend.

questions.question: Why was Mr. Ito often alone?
questions.explanation: 妻を亡くし、一人で過ごしていたからです。

questions.question: What did Hana do at first?
questions.explanation: Hana は昼食に誘いました。

questions.question: Why did Hana add one more chair?
options: Someone else might need a friend.
questions.explanation: 他にも友達を必要とする人がいると考えたためです。

stories.title: The Red Umbrella
stories.subtitle: 赤い傘
stories.description: An act of kindness travels farther than its owner expects.

scenes.text: On a rainy morning, Sora missed his bus and stood outside the station. He had left his umbrella at home and was afraid of being late for school.
scenes.ja: 雨の朝、ソラはバスに乗り遅れ、駅の外に立っていました。傘を家に忘れ、学校に遅れることを心配していました。
scenes.alt: A student waits in heavy rain at a station without an umbrella.

grammar.focus: Sora missed his bus and stood outside the station.
grammar.note: and は2つの動作 missed と stood を結びます。

scenes.text: A woman he did not know held out a bright red umbrella. “Take this,” she said. “You can give it to someone else when they need it.”
scenes.ja: 見知らぬ女性が鮮やかな赤い傘を差し出しました。「これを使って」と彼女は言いました。「必要としている別の人に渡してくれればいいのよ」。
scenes.alt: Kind stranger hands Sora a bright red umbrella.

grammar.focus: You can give it to someone else when they need it.
grammar.note: when は「～するとき」の時を表す接続詞です。give A to B の形も確認しましょう。

scenes.text: For several weeks, Sora carried the umbrella in his school bag. He wanted to return it, but he never met the woman again.
scenes.ja: それから何週間か、ソラは傘を通学かばんに入れて持ち歩きました。返したかったのですが、その女性には二度と会えませんでした。
scenes.alt: Sora keeps the folded red umbrella carefully in his school bag.

grammar.focus: He wanted to return it, but he never met the woman again.

parts.value: but he never met the woman again

grammar.note: want to + 動詞の原形 は「～したい」。but は逆接です。

scenes.text: One afternoon, he noticed a little girl crying near a bus stop. Her shoes were wet, and she could not find her mother.
scenes.ja: ある午後、ソラはバス停の近くで泣いている小さな女の子に気づきました。靴は濡れ、母親が見つからず困っていました。
scenes.alt: A young girl cries by a rainy bus stop as Sora approaches.

grammar.focus: he noticed a little girl crying near a bus stop.
grammar.note: notice + 人 + ～ing は「人が～していることに気づく」です。

scenes.text: Sora shared the umbrella and helped her find the station office. Soon her mother arrived, relieved to see her daughter safe.
scenes.ja: ソラは傘に入れてあげ、駅の事務室を探すのを手伝いました。まもなく母親が到着し、娘の無事を見て安心しました。
scenes.alt: Sora shelters the girl under the red umbrella outside the station office.

grammar.focus: her mother arrived, relieved to see her daughter safe.

parts.value: relieved to see her daughter safe

grammar.note: relieved は母親の気持ちを後ろから補足しています。to see は感情の原因を表します。

scenes.text: When Sora offered the girl the red umbrella, she asked, “Will I ever see you again?” He smiled. “Maybe not. But you can keep the kindness going.”
scenes.ja: ソラが女の子に赤い傘を渡すと、彼女は「また会えるかな」と尋ねました。ソラは微笑みました。「会えないかもしれない。でも、優しさは次の人につなげられるよ」。
scenes.alt: The girl holds the red umbrella; Sora waves goodbye under clearing skies.

grammar.focus: you can keep the kindness going.
grammar.note: keep + 目的語 + ～ing は「～を続けさせる」という意味を作ります。

vocab.detail: miss the bus で「バスに乗り遅れる」。
hold something out（物を差し出す）。
return something to someone と表せます。
notice + 人 + ～ing は人の動作への気づき。
be relieved to ...「～して安心する」。
vocab.example: She was relieved to see her.

vocab.detail: offer A B / offer B to A の形があります。
keep + 目的語 + going で「途切れないようにする」。

questions.question: Why could Sora not stay dry at the station?
questions.explanation: 傘を家に置いてきたためです。

questions.question: What did the woman tell Sora?
options: To pass the umbrella to someone in need.
To take it to the police.
questions.explanation: 困っている別の人に渡すように言いました。

questions.question: What is the main message?
questions.explanation: 優しさの連鎖が主題です。

stories.title: The Box of Letters
stories.subtitle: 手紙の箱
stories.description: A teenager discovers a friendship that time could not erase.

scenes.text: While cleaning her grandfather's room, Mei discovered a wooden box full of letters. Each envelope carried the same address, but none of them had been sent.
scenes.ja: 祖父の部屋を掃除していたメイは、手紙でいっぱいの木箱を見つけました。封筒にはすべて同じ住所が書かれていましたが、一通も投函されていませんでした。
scenes.alt: Mei discovers an old wooden box of unsent handwritten letters.

grammar.focus: While cleaning her grandfather's room, Mei discovered a wooden box full of letters.

parts.value: a wooden box full of letters

grammar.note: While cleaning は While she was cleaning の省略形で、主語が共通のときに使います。

scenes.text: The letters were addressed to Ken, her grandfather's closest childhood friend. The two boys had promised to meet again after their families moved to different cities.
scenes.ja: 手紙は祖父の幼なじみで親友だったケンに宛てられていました。少年だった二人は、家族が別々の町へ引っ越した後、再会を約束していました。
scenes.alt: Close-up of an old letter addressed to Ken alongside a faded childhood photo.

grammar.focus: The two boys had promised to meet again after their families moved to different cities.

parts.value: after their families moved to different cities

grammar.note: had promised は過去完了。引っ越し後の出来事より前の約束を表します。

scenes.text: However, her grandfather had never found the courage to write about his difficult life. The letters described small victories, painful losses, and the hope of reconnecting.
scenes.ja: しかし祖父は、自分の苦労の多い人生を知らせる勇気を持てずにいたのです。手紙には小さな成功やつらい喪失、再会への希望が綴られていました。
scenes.alt: Mei reads the handwritten letters beside a window with gentle afternoon light.

grammar.focus: her grandfather had never found the courage to write about his difficult life.

parts.value: to write about his difficult life

grammar.note: the courage to do は「～する勇気」。to不定詞が名詞 courage を説明します。

scenes.text: Mei asked her grandfather whether he still wanted to see Ken. He hesitated, then whispered, “I thought it was too late.” She decided to search for the address.
scenes.ja: メイが今でもケンに会いたいか尋ねると、祖父はためらい、「もう遅いと思っていた」とささやきました。メイは住所を探すことに決めました。
scenes.alt: Grandfather looks uncertain while Mei gently offers to help him reconnect.

grammar.focus: Mei asked her grandfather whether he still wanted to see Ken.

parts.value: whether he still wanted to see Ken

grammar.note: whether 節は「～かどうか」。asked の内容を表す間接疑問です。

scenes.text: With help from a local community center, she finally contacted Ken's family. The old friends met in a quiet park and spoke for hours, as though they had never been apart.
scenes.ja: 地域の交流センターの協力で、メイはついにケンの家族に連絡しました。二人は静かな公園で再会し、離れ離れだったことなどなかったかのように何時間も話しました。
scenes.alt: Two elderly childhood friends embrace in a quiet park, Mei watching happily.

grammar.focus: The old friends met in a quiet park and spoke for hours, as though they had never been apart.

parts.value: in a quiet park / for hours
as though they had never been apart

grammar.note: as though + 過去完了は「まるで過去に～でなかったかのように」という仮定表現です。

scenes.text: On the way home, her grandfather held the empty wooden box and smiled. “I kept every letter because I was afraid,” he said. “You helped me finally send the most important message: I never forgot you.”
scenes.ja: 帰り道、祖父は空になった木箱を抱いて微笑みました。「怖くて手紙を全部取っておいたんだ」と言いました。「でも君のおかげで一番大事な気持ちを伝えられた。ずっと忘れていなかったよ、と」。
scenes.alt: Grandfather carries the empty letter box beside Mei at sunset.

grammar.focus: “I kept every letter because I was afraid,”
grammar.note: because 以下が「なぜ手紙を保管したか」という理由を示します。

vocab.detail: letter（手紙）を入れる外側の紙袋。
be addressed to 人 で「人に宛てられている」。
vocab.example: The letter was addressed to Ken.

vocab.detail: find the courage to do で「～する勇気を出す」。
vocab.example: He found the courage to speak.

vocab.detail: connect に re- が付き「再びつながる」。
hesitate to do で「～するのをためらう」。
contact someone は前置詞なしで目的語を取ります。
事実と異なることにも使われる表現。
vocab.example: They talked as though nothing had changed.

questions.question: Why were the letters not sent?
options: Grandfather felt unable to share his struggles.
questions.explanation: 祖父は難しい人生を語る勇気を持てなかったからです。

questions.question: How did Mei locate Ken?
questions.explanation: 地域の交流センターが協力しました。

questions.question: What does the empty box symbolize?
questions.explanation: 伝えられなかった気持ちが届いたことを象徴しています。

stories.title: The Piano in the Hall
stories.subtitle: ホールのピアノ
stories.description: Music restores a connection that grief had silenced.

scenes.text: For years, a dusty piano stood in the entrance hall of a small hospital. Nobody remembered when it had last been played, and the staff considered removing it to create more space.
scenes.ja: 小さな病院の玄関ホールには、何年もほこりをかぶったピアノが置かれていました。最後に演奏された時を知る人もおらず、職員たちは場所を空けるため撤去を検討していました。
scenes.alt: An old dusty upright piano stands alone in a quiet hospital lobby.

grammar.focus: the staff considered removing it to create more space.
grammar.note: consider は目的語に動名詞を取ります。目的を表す to 不定詞にも注目します。

scenes.text: During a volunteer visit, seventeen-year-old Rina noticed the instrument and gently pressed a key. Its uneven sound reminded her of the evenings she had spent practicing beside her grandmother.
scenes.ja: ボランティアで訪れた17歳のリナはピアノに気づき、そっと鍵盤を押しました。不揃いな音を聞き、祖母のそばで練習した夜を思い出しました。
scenes.alt: Rina presses an old piano key and remembers her grandmother teaching music.

grammar.focus: Its uneven sound reminded her of the evenings she had spent practicing beside her grandmother.

parts.value: of the evenings she had spent practicing beside her grandmother

grammar.note: remind A of B は「AにBを思い出させる」。she had spent は evenings を説明します。

scenes.text: Her grandmother had gradually lost the ability to speak after a stroke, yet she could still recognize familiar melodies. Whenever Rina played, her grandmother's fingers would move softly along with the music.
scenes.ja: 祖母は脳卒中の後、徐々に話す力を失いましたが、聞き慣れた旋律を認識することはできました。リナが弾くたび、祖母の指は音楽に合わせて優しく動いたのでした。
scenes.alt: Tender memory of an elderly grandmother moving her fingers to Rina's piano.

grammar.focus: Whenever Rina played, her grandmother's fingers would move softly along with the music.
grammar.note: 過去の習慣を表す would。whenever は「～するたびに」です。

scenes.text: Rina persuaded the hospital to let her organize a small restoration project. Local musicians donated their time, and a technician volunteered to repair the neglected instrument.
scenes.ja: リナは病院を説得して、小さな修復活動を企画する許可を得ました。地元の音楽家たちが時間を提供し、調律師が放置されていた楽器の修理を申し出ました。
scenes.alt: Rina and a piano technician restore the instrument with volunteer helpers.

grammar.focus: Rina persuaded the hospital to let her organize a small restoration project.

parts.value: to let her organize a small restoration project

grammar.note: persuade A to do は「Aを説得して～させる」。let + 人 + 動詞の原形にも注目。

scenes.text: On the day of the first performance, patients and visitors gathered in the hall. An elderly man who rarely left his room asked to sit near the piano, saying the song reminded him of his late wife.
scenes.ja: 最初の演奏の日、患者や来訪者がホールに集まりました。普段はほとんど部屋を出ない高齢の男性が、亡き妻を思い出す曲だと言ってピアノの近くに座りたがりました。
scenes.alt: Patients and staff gather around the restored piano as Rina performs.

grammar.focus: An elderly man who rarely left his room asked to sit near the piano, saying the song reminded him of his late wife.

parts.value: An elderly man who rarely left his room
saying the song reminded him of his late wife

grammar.note: who rarely left his room は an elderly man を修飾する関係詞節です。

scenes.text: As the final notes faded, the man quietly thanked Rina. She realized that the piano had not simply been repaired; it had become a place where memories could be shared, even when words were no longer enough.
scenes.ja: 最後の音が消えると、男性は静かにリナに感謝しました。リナは、ピアノは単に修理されただけでなく、言葉では足りない時にも思い出を分かち合える場所になったのだと悟りました。
scenes.alt: The elderly man thanks Rina at the piano; people share a moving moment.

grammar.focus: it had become a place where memories could be shared, even when words were no longer enough.

parts.value: even when words were no longer enough

grammar.note: where は先行詞 a place を説明する関係副詞。could be shared は受動態です。

vocab.detail: 音楽を演奏するための道具を表します。
even（均一な）に否定の接頭辞 un- が付いた語。
vocab.example: The piano made an uneven sound.

vocab.detail: 医療文脈では脳卒中、一般には一打・一筆などの意味も。
persuade A to do の構文。
vocab.example: Rina persuaded the staff to help.

vocab.detail: restore（修復する）の名詞形。
neglect（放置する）から。
fade away で「次第に消える」。
状態の変化を強調します。

questions.question: Why did the piano matter to Rina?
options: It reminded her of her grandmother.
It belonged to a famous musician.
questions.explanation: 祖母と過ごした記憶を呼び起こしたためです。

questions.question: How was the restoration made possible?
questions.explanation: 地域の音楽家や技術者の協力によります。

questions.question: What is the deeper meaning of the ending?
options: Music can connect people beyond words.
questions.explanation: 言葉を越えた記憶とつながりが主題です。

stories.title: The Lighthouse We Kept
stories.subtitle: 私たちが守った灯台
stories.description: A coastal town learns that rebuilding means preserving its stories.

scenes.text: After the devastating storm, the coastal town of Aoba resembled a place abruptly erased from the map. Houses stood roofless, fishing boats lay scattered inland, and the old lighthouse had ceased to function.
scenes.ja: 壊滅的な嵐の後、海辺の青葉町は地図から突然消し去られた場所のようでした。家々の屋根は失われ、漁船は陸地に散乱し、古い灯台は機能を停止していました。
scenes.alt: Storm-damaged coastal village with an unlit lighthouse above scattered fishing boats.

grammar.focus: After the devastating storm, the coastal town of Aoba resembled a place abruptly erased from the map.

parts.value: a place abruptly erased from the map

grammar.note: resemble は他動詞で前置詞は不要。erased は過去分詞による後置修飾です。

scenes.text: Officials proposed demolishing the lighthouse, arguing that its restoration would divert resources from urgently needed housing. For many residents, however, the structure represented something no financial estimate could adequately capture.
scenes.ja: 行政担当者は、灯台の修復は緊急に必要な住宅への資源を奪うとして、取り壊しを提案しました。しかし多くの住民にとって、その建造物には金銭的な見積もりでは到底捉えきれない意味がありました。
scenes.alt: Town meeting where residents debate whether to preserve the damaged lighthouse.

grammar.focus: Officials proposed demolishing the lighthouse, arguing that its restoration would divert resources from urgently needed housing.

parts.value: arguing that its restoration would divert resources from urgently needed housing

grammar.note: propose の目的語は動名詞。arguing ... は同時に行う発言内容を補足する分詞構文です。

scenes.text: Among those who objected was sixteen-year-old Nao, whose grandfather had maintained the light for four decades. He had once told her that its purpose was not merely to warn vessels of danger, but to reassure those at sea that someone was waiting for them.
scenes.ja: 反対した人々の中には、祖父が40年間灯台を守ってきた16歳のナオがいました。祖父はかつて、灯台の役割は船に危険を知らせるだけでなく、海にいる人々に「待っている人がいる」と安心させることだと話していました。
scenes.alt: Nao holds her grandfather's weathered notebook at the damaged lighthouse.

grammar.focus: Among those who objected was sixteen-year-old Nao, whose grandfather had maintained the light for four decades.

parts.value: whose grandfather had maintained the light for four decades

grammar.note: 場所・範囲を表す語句が文頭に来た倒置文。通常の語順は Sixteen-year-old Nao was among ... です。

scenes.text: Rather than launch an emotional appeal alone, Nao interviewed surviving fishermen and recorded stories of rescues, homecomings, and relatives who had kept vigil through countless nights. She assembled the testimonies into a digital archive, making the community's collective memory visible.
scenes.ja: 感情的な訴えだけに頼るのではなく、ナオは生還した漁師に取材し、救助や帰港、幾夜も見守り続けた家族の物語を記録しました。証言をデジタル資料にまとめ、地域の集合的な記憶を見える形にしたのです。
scenes.alt: Nao records elderly fishermen telling personal stories in a temporary community center.

grammar.focus: Rather than launch an emotional appeal alone, Nao interviewed surviving fishermen and recorded stories of rescues, homecomings, and relatives who had kept vigil through countless nights.

parts.value: Rather than launch an emotional appeal alone
surviving fishermen / stories of rescues, homecomings, and relatives
who had kept vigil through countless nights

grammar.note: rather than + 動詞原形 は「～するよりむしろ」。interview は他動詞です。

scenes.text: Her project gradually changed the discussion: the question was no longer whether the lighthouse justified its expense, but how the town could safeguard its heritage while rebuilding responsibly. Volunteers and engineers devised a modest plan that preserved the tower and restored its beacon.
scenes.ja: 彼女の活動で議論は次第に変わりました。灯台が費用に見合うかではなく、責任ある復興と地域の遺産保護をどう両立するかが問われるようになったのです。ボランティアと技術者は塔を残し、灯りを復旧する現実的な計画を考案しました。
scenes.alt: Engineers and volunteers carefully repair the old coastal lighthouse together.

grammar.focus: the question was no longer whether the lighthouse justified its expense, but how the town could safeguard its heritage while rebuilding responsibly.

parts.value: no longer whether the lighthouse justified its expense, but how the town could safeguard its heritage while rebuilding responsibly

grammar.note: not ... but ... と対比構造。whether と how に導かれる名詞節が補語として並列されています。

scenes.text: When the beacon finally illuminated the harbor, Nao stood beside her grandfather, who could barely contain his tears. The light could not undo the catastrophe, yet it affirmed something the storm had failed to destroy: the bonds through which a community recognizes itself.
scenes.ja: やがて灯台の光が港を照らした時、ナオは涙をこらえきれない祖父の隣に立っていました。その光は災害をなかったことにはできません。しかし嵐でも壊せなかったもの――地域が自分たちの存在を確かめ合う人と人の絆――を確かに示していたのでした。
scenes.alt: Restored lighthouse illuminates the harbor as Nao and grandfather embrace at dusk.

grammar.focus: The light could not undo the catastrophe, yet it affirmed something the storm had failed to destroy: the bonds through which a community recognizes itself.

parts.value: the catastrophe / something the storm had failed to destroy: the bonds through which a community recognizes itself
the storm had failed to destroy

grammar.note: yet による逆接。the storm had failed to destroy は something を説明する関係詞が省略された節です。

vocab.detail: devastate（荒廃させる）から生まれた語。
建物を意図的に解体すること。

vocab.ja: 転用する、方向を変える
vocab.detail: divert resources from A to B は資源を移すこと。
adequate（十分な）の副詞。
vocab.example: No estimate could adequately capture it.

vocab.detail: reassure A that ... の形。
複数形 testimonies。
危険や損失から守ること。
vocab.example: They wanted to safeguard their heritage.

vocab.ja: 受け継いだ文化的遺産
vocab.detail: 建築物だけでなく記憶や伝統も含みます。
vocab.example: The lighthouse was part of their heritage.

vocab.detail: 存在や価値を強く確認すること。

vocab.ja: 元に戻す、なかったことにする
vocab.detail: 過去の出来事を取り消す意味にも用います。

questions.question: Why did officials oppose restoration?
options: They wanted funds prioritized for urgent housing.
They thought the beacon was too bright.
They wanted to build a museum.
questions.explanation: 住宅再建のための資源を優先する必要があると考えたからです。

questions.question: What was distinctive about Nao's strategy?
options: She gathered testimony and created an archive.
She rebuilt the tower by herself.
questions.explanation: 具体的な証言を可視化し、議論の前提を変えました。

questions.question: What does the final light primarily symbolize?
options: The total reversal of the disaster.
questions.explanation: 災害にも失われなかった共同体のつながりを象徴します。
